caption: I budgeted R900 for eating out this month. It's R1 800. Low season does something to my willpower — anyone else eat their feelings when bookings are quiet?

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: Cottage near the harbour, water, refuse
slides.body: Rent doesn't drop just because the tourists have.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: Needed for airport pickups and my own commute
slides.body: Fixed every month, high season or dead quiet like this one.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Just for me, cooking more since the guesthouse kitchen's quiet
slides.body: Slightly up this month. Comfort eating apparently has a line item now.

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.includes: Hospital plan, no gap cover yet
slides.body: The one bill that doesn't care what season it is either.

slides.title: Eating out & coffee
slides.includes: Takeaways on the slow days I couldn't face cooking for one
slides.body: I budgeted R900 for this at the start of the month. It's exactly double.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Car insurance, cellphone & data, funeral policy, streaming, stokvel
slides.body: Five small debits that don't care that bookings are down.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R16 200. High season me would laugh at this number. Low season me is just glad it's not negative.

slides.title: I finally saw where the plan and the month didn't match
slides.body:
I set this month's budget in Beyond Horizon before it started, then let it compare that against my statement once the month ended. Eating out was exactly double what I'd planned.

No bank login needed.
